Task class: Assert description is non-null and non-empty
commitResults.messageBody:
Every caller that constructs a Task subclass (Todo, Deadline,
Event) does so only after Parser has already validated the
description via a JimboException, so an empty description
reaching this constructor should never happen if the rest of
the program is correct.

The assertion documents that trust boundary explicitly. If a
future code path ever constructs a Task without going through
Parser's validation first, this will fail loudly during testing
instead of silently producing a task with a blank description
that only becomes confusing later, e.g. in Ui output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser class: Assert index is in bounds after parseTaskIndex
commitResults.messageBody:
parseTaskIndex() already throws a JimboException when the user
types an out-of-range task number, so the assertion added here
is not for catching bad user input — that case is already
handled above it.

Instead, it documents an internal postcondition: if the method
returns without throwing, the returned index is guaranteed
valid. This distinguishes assertions (checking assumptions a
correct program should never violate) from exceptions (handling
conditions a correct program can still encounter, like bad
input), which is easy to conflate.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage class: Assert task is assigned after the type switch
commitResults.messageBody:
Every case in parseLine()'s switch on typeIcon either assigns
task (T, D, E) or throws a JimboException (default, and the
field-count checks inside each case), so task is guaranteed
non-null by the time execution reaches the line after the
switch. That guarantee isn't obvious without tracing all four
branches, though.

The assertion makes it explicit and machine-checked. If a
future case is ever added that forgets to assign task or throw,
this fails loudly during testing instead of surfacing as a
NullPointerException a few lines later, on task.markAsDone(),
with a less informative stack trace.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList class: Assert index is caller-validated in get/remove
commitResults.messageBody:
get() and remove() delegate straight to the underlying
ArrayList, which already throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on a
bad index, so this assertion adds no new runtime protection.

What it documents is a design decision: TaskList trusts its
caller to have already validated the index (in practice, always
via Parser.parseTaskIndex()) rather than re-validating it itself
and throwing a JimboException, which would duplicate work Parser
already does.

If a future caller ever bypasses that validation, this fails
during testing with a message pointing at the actual violated
assumption, rather than relying on ArrayList's generic
IndexOutOfBoundsException to explain the same thing indirectly.
